frames.narration: A client opens a connection to a Cloudflare IP address. Its first packet is a SYN, the packet that starts a TCP connection. The router sends it to some server, here Server 1. With ECMP, any server may get any packet, and the data center does not need to know which.

On Server 1 the XDP programs run before the kernel's network stack. First l4drop, which would drop an attack packet. This one passes. Then Unimog hashes the packet's 4-tuple (source and destination address and port) and uses the low bits of the hash to pick a bucket of the forwarding table. The bucket's first slot names Server A, and its second slot is empty.

Unimog wraps the packet in new headers addressed to Server A, so the original destination address is kept, and sends it back out. Server A's redirector sees a SYN, which is always handled on the first-hop server. The connection is set up on Server A.

Hours later an operator drains Server A for maintenance. The conductor builds a new table. In each bucket that named A, the first slot now names another server (B for this bucket) and the second slot keeps A. The table travels through Consul to xdpd on every server. New connections will go to B, and nothing is said to the old connections.

messages.label: new table via Consul and xdpd: first B, second A

frames.narration: The client sends another packet on the same connection. The router sends it to whichever server it likes, and every server has the same table. The bucket now says first B, second A, and the packet is wrapped for B, with A's address carried in an extension header.

Server B's redirector checks: not a SYN, and B has no socket for this connection. So instead of answering with a reset, it forwards the packet on to Server A, using the address from the extension header.

Server A has the socket and processes the packet, and the connection carries on, even though A is being drained. A brand new connection that hashes to this bucket would start with a SYN and stay on B. When the old connections on A have ended, A has nothing left to do and can be taken out of service.
